sourceFile: https://friendsofnavajoland.org/prayer-cycle/ (fetched directly; the diocese's own live page, not a downloaded document)
notes: This source is the support organization Friends of Navajoland's own page, not a page hosted by Navajoland/ECN itself, but its prayer-chart content is the diocese/mission's own published cycle. `diocese` uses the exact self-identification the chart itself prints in its own Sunday entry, "Episcopal Church in Navajoland" (no leading "The"), rather than "Friends of Navajoland" (the hosting organization) or a invented fuller form.

cycleType 'day-of-week-recurring' was added to this schema specifically for this file, per Josh's direct decision 2026-09-30 ("a different prayer daily, repeating every 7 days") -- see schema.json's own `rules` for the full record. `weekday` follows JavaScript's own Date.getDay() numbering (Sunday=0 ... Saturday=6).

The source is a 7-row, 6-column table ("Days", then "Our Mission Congregations", "Our Active Clergy and Lay Pastors", "Our Churches", "Our Lay Staff and Volunteers", "Our Special Projects/Ministries"), fetched directly and parsed from the raw HTML <table> markup (confirmed via BeautifulSoup, and cross-checked against the live rendered page, which required force-overriding an inline `visibility: hidden` style the WP Table Builder plugin applies before its own JS runs -- likely blocked in this sandbox the same way an external font CDN is elsewhere in this project). Each day's five columns are recorded here as five (or more, after splitting -- see below) `category` subjects, each disclosing which column it came from in its own `note` only when that context isn't otherwise obvious.

None of the five columns' content is typed `parish` in this file, even where a cell names an actual church -- unlike this corpus's usual diocese-level files, nothing in this source ever comma-separates a congregation's name from its own town/chapter, so a `parish`/`place` split would mean inferring structure the source doesn't provide. All entries are `category` throughout, including the "Our Churches" column.

Several cells in the source's own raw HTML concatenate two or more people/churches/phrases into one run-on string with NO delimiter at all between them (no comma, semicolon, line break, or other punctuation) -- confirmed by inspecting the table's own markup directly, not just a lossy text extraction. Where a clear boundary exists (most often a repeated title word like "Rev."/"Lay Pastor", or an unambiguous second church name), these were split into separate subjects as a disclosed judgment call, with the split reasoning noted on the affected subject(s); this is the single most common class of disclosure in this file.

Per the TEC roster's own research note, the diocesan bishop's office is currently vacant (Bishop Barry Beisner's ministry ended June 21, 2026, per Navajoland's own announcement) and the Standing Committee now serves as ecclesiastical authority -- the source's own Monday entry still names Bishop Beisner and has not been updated to reflect the vacancy; preserved as printed rather than corrected or removed, with the vacancy disclosed on that specific subject.

A few names carry disclosed spelling inconsistencies within the source itself, preserved exactly as printed rather than harmonized: "St. Christopher's Mission" (Thursday's own Churches column) versus "St. Christophers Mission" (no apostrophe, in that same day's and Friday's Special Projects columns).
